blindSummary:
A 2023 law makes the legal environment here exceptionally dangerous for trans visitors: it imposes life imprisonment for same-sex conduct and the death penalty for aggravated forms of it, and a foreign government's travel advisory explicitly warns that "the law applies to both visitors and residents". Over 1,000 rights violations (arrests, torture, evictions) were documented in nine months. Mobs have gathered outside trans people's homes (one woman described being grabbed and shouted at that she needed to die); police use digital entrapment (obtaining evidence via dating apps); and the government has been found to "spread misinformation and hatred against LGBT people". The law also criminalises the "promotion" of same-sex relations — meaning any advocacy or support is banned.

There are no laws regulating gender identity as such — the 2023 law targets same-sex conduct and "promotion", not trans identity per se — but trans people are swept up in the broader anti-LGBT crackdown, mobs and state violence. The constitutional court upheld the law in April 2024 (striking down only a few provisions on healthcare access and renting).

The death penalty is confined to "aggravated" cases of same-sex conduct — unlike some states where it formally reaches all same-sex conduct, and unlike others where gender expression itself is the written offence — and no trans-specific killing of a visitor or border-targeting is documented; the systematic, state-led crackdown nonetheless means any risk of discovery carries extreme consequences.
blindOutOfScope: Terrorism linked to insurgent groups in remote border areas, violent crime (armed robbery, sexual assault), and civil unrest affect all travellers; only trans-specific risk is assessed here.
blindSourceSummaries: International human-rights organisation report (May 2025): how this country's anti-LGBT climate unleashes abuse - the 2023 law (death penalty for aggravated same-sex conduct, lengthy sentences for 'promotion') has fuelled arrests, raids on shelters, evictions and public outings; many LGBT people in hiding; a small group of mothers began speaking publicly in support of their LGBT children.
An international rights group (Apr 2024): this country's constitutional court upholds the 2023 anti-homosexuality law with life-sentence provisions intact.
NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying news-agency report (June 2024) covers rights violations against this country's LGBTQ community escalating, per an advocacy group.

Foreign broadsheet (Jan 2024): fear stalks the country over its brutal anti-gay law - a headline conveying that simply going outside makes one a target; profiles a resident of a safe house holding 20 other transgender people on the outskirts of the capital.
NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying foreign-government travel advisory for this country includes LGBT-specific warnings at its highest warning level.
Digital-rights organisation analysis: how digital entrapment and surveillance are used against LGBTQ people under the 2023 law's framework.

International human-rights organisation (Oct 2024): criminalisation shrinks online civic space for LGBTQ people here - a report on people being forced to lead double online lives documents technology-facilitated gender-based violence (doxing, outing, threats, blackmail, impersonation, hacking, disinformation); the 2023 law fostered a climate of impunity, forcing individuals and organisations to alter how they engage online.

A newswire report (Feb 2026): police in a provincial city detained two women reported by neighbours for same-sex intimacy — among the first known arrests under this country's 2023 anti-homosexuality law.

A foreign government's 2011 human-rights report on this country: the three most important problems included 'violence and discrimination against marginalized groups' - naming women, children, persons with disabilities and the lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender community - from the era of the earlier anti-homosexuality bill debates.
blindTangential: The 2023 law's life imprisonment and death penalty for aggravated same-sex conduct apply to visitors — a direct risk for trans visitors with partners or perceived as same-sex-active; dating-app entrapment is a direct app-user risk.
